subtitle: When Solanki stone learned to follow the sun

panels.shot: dramatic sunrise wide, low angle from temple steps toward glowing horizon
panels.action: Bhima I & the Modhera Sthapatis stand on the half-built plinth of the Sun Temple, silhouettes against a blazing dawn as the first rays spear straight down the temple axis toward the dark, waiting sanctum.

dialogue.text: In Bhima I’s Gujarat, at Modhera on the Pushpavati, sthapatis dared a question: can stone be taught to read the sun?

i18n.hi: भीम देव के गुजरात में, पुष्पावती के किनारे मोढेरा पर, स्थापतियों ने हिम्मत से पूछा: क्या पत्थर को सूरज पढ़ना सिखाया जा सकता है?

panels.shot: bird's-eye over landscape, river and village with marked temple site
panels.action: From high above, Bhima I & the Modhera Sthapatis survey a bend of the Pushpavati River, scrubland and low fields, while attendants hold simple surveying ropes and poles at a chosen rise.

dialogue.text: Around 1026–27, when records speak of Bhima I on the Solanki throne, a sacred bend of the Pushpavati was marked for a new Surya temple.

i18n.hi: लगभग १०२६–२७ में, जब लेखों में चालुक्य सिंहासन पर भीम प्रथम का नाम है, पुष्पावती की एक पवित्र मोड़ पर नए सूर्य मंदिर की जगह ठहरी।

panels.shot: medium shot at eye level, council-like gathering
panels.action: In a tented pavilion, Bhima I sits on a simple low throne, listening as the chief sthapati unrolls a palm-leaf plan, other artisans and priests gathered with attentive, serious faces.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions on the great kunda step speak of donors, but not of the first idea. Scholars read the plan through stone: a kunda, a sabhamandapa, a garbhagriha, all held on a single solar line.

i18n.hi: महाकुंड की सीढ़ियों पर शिलालेख दानियों के नाम गाते हैं, पर पहली कल्पना का नहीं। विद्वान पत्थर से योजना पढ़ते हैं: एक कुंड, एक सभामंडप, एक गर्भगृह, सब एक ही सूर्य रेखा पर जड़े।

panels.shot: close-up on chief sthapati's hands with instruments
panels.action: The Modhera Sthapati kneels on bare ground, tracing a straight line with a cord and peg while an assistant holds a gnomon stick casting a sharp shadow, simple measuring knots visible on the cord.

dialogue.text: No medieval manual from Modhera explains their method, yet the layout tells its own tale: cords, stakes and shadow-sticks caught the east–west line long before stone was set.

i18n.hi: मोढेरा से कोई मध्ययुगीन ग्रंथ उनकी तरकीब नहीं समझाता, पर नक्शा खुद कहानी कहता है: रस्सियाँ, खूंटे और छाया डंडे ने पत्थर से बहुत पहले पूरब–पश्चिम रेखा पकड़ ली थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of foundation trenches and emerging stepped tank
panels.action: A wide view shows labourers cutting the first steps of the future kunda, rectangular trenches filling with groundwater, while beyond, marked axes indicate where the mandapa and sanctum will rise.

dialogue.text: First, the earth was opened for water. The great stepped kunda took shape, each tier of steps and landings planned to hold shrines and donors’ dreams in orderly rows.

i18n.hi: पहले धरती जल के लिए खोदी गई। विशाल सीढ़ीदार कुंड उभरा, हर पायदान और चौकटी ऐसी गढ़ी कि देवालय और दानियों के सपने कतारों में जड़ सकें।

panels.shot: angled view along kunda edge towards future temple axis
panels.action: Standing on the emerging edge of the kunda, the Sthapati sights along a line of placed stones toward the slightly higher ground where the sabhamandapa plinth is being squared, Bhima watching from shade.

dialogue.text: Dhaky’s careful measurements show the three—tank, hall and sanctum—held in a near-straight axis. Water to west, audience hall in between, the dark womb of Surya’s shrine at the end.

i18n.hi: ढाकी के नाप बताते हैं: तीनों—कुंड, सभा और गर्भ—लगभग एक सीध में हैं। पश्चिम में जल, बीच में सभा, अंत में सूर्य के गर्भ का अँधेरा।

panels.shot: low interior shot inside rising sabhamandapa, columns framing sky
panels.action: Within the half-built sabhamandapa, carved pillars already stand in rows, framing a rectangle of sky aligned with the distant sunrise point, the Sthapati gesturing to younger craftsmen at the alignment.

dialogue.text: The sabhamandapa was no casual hall. Its doorways and columns were lined so that, on certain mornings, the path of light would run undisturbed from horizon to sanctum.

i18n.hi: सभामंडप कोई साधारण हल नहीं था। उसके द्वार और स्तंभ ऐसे साधे गए कि कुछ सुबहों को रोशनी की धारा क्षितिज से गर्भ तक बिना टूटे दौड़ सके।

panels.shot: tight interior of sanctum doorway from inside looking out
panels.action: From deep inside the dim, unfinished sanctum, the viewer peers out through the doorway as the Sthapati and an assistant stand framed outside, checking the door jambs with plumb lines, sunrise direction beyond.

dialogue.text: Today, observers stand where the murti once stood and see it: at equinox sunrise, the first beam slips perfectly through the doorway, along the floor, into the heart of the shrine.

i18n.hi: आज दर्शक वहीं खड़े होते हैं जहाँ कभी मूर्ति थी, और देखते हैं: विषुव के सूर्योदय पर पहली किरण दरवाज़े से सीधे फर्श पर सरकती, गर्भ के हृदय में घुसती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Bhima and sthapati watching dawn inside sanctum mockup
panels.action: Bhima I and the Sthapati stand in a simple wooden frame that marks the future sanctum doorway at dawn, watching a shaft of light fall exactly where a small stone marks the intended pedestal.

dialogue.speaker: bhima_i_and_the_modhera_sthapatis
dialogue.text: When the sun and the stone agree, we shall build.

i18n.hi: जब सूरज और पत्थर एक मत हो जाएँ, तभी मंदिर उठेगा।

panels.shot: wide shot of completed kunda with many small shrines
panels.action: The finished stepped kunda stretches out, its terraces crowded with dozens of small shrines and niches, each sheltering a deity image, townsfolk descending the steps with offerings and water pots.

dialogue.text: Around the water, about 108 small shrines, say modern counts, waited in tiers—an echo of sacred number, each niche another point where sky, stone and devotion could meet.

i18n.hi: जल के चारों ओर, आज की गिनती में लगभग १०८ छोटे देवालय, तह–दर–तह बैठे थे—एक पवित्र संख्या की गूँज, हर कोना आसमान, पत्थर और भक्ति के मिलने की जगह।

panels.shot: close-up montage of twelve solar deities carved in niches
panels.action: A sequence-like frame shows twelve different Surya forms carved in niches along the temple walls, each slightly varied in posture and attendant figures, sunlight grazing their sharp sandstone carvings.

dialogue.text: On the temple itself, scholars count twelve principal solar panels. Surya is shown in many moods, as if each month or station in the year found its own image in stone.

i18n.hi: मंदिर की देह पर विद्वान बारह प्रधान सूर्य पट्ट गिनते हैं। सूर्य कई भावों में उकेरा है, जैसे हर महीना, हर पड़ाव अपनी अलग मूर्ति पाता हो।

panels.shot: medium shot of scholar-like sthapati pointing to zodiacal carving
panels.action: The Sthapati, older now, runs his fingers over a frieze of dancers and celestial figures, some bearing clear solar discs and perhaps signs, watching young apprentices study the sequence with curiosity.

dialogue.text: Some modern writers see in these bands the march of seasons and stars. The record is silent, yet the careful repetition of solar forms suggests more than simple ornament.

i18n.hi: कुछ आधुनिक लेखक इन पट्टों में ऋतुओं और तारों की चाल पढ़ते हैं। अभिलेख चुप हैं, पर सूर्य रूपों की सधी हुई पुनरावृत्ति साधारण सजावट से ज्यादा कहती है।

panels.shot: long shot at solstice noon, temple casting precise shadow near kunda
panels.action: At high noon, the temple’s profile throws a sharp, compact shadow that just kisses a marked edge near the kunda, the Sthapati squinting up, apprentices marking the shadow tip with small stones.

dialogue.text: Bhatnagar and Livingston note another quiet trick: at solstice, the temple’s body and shadow behave with surprising precision. The stone seems to measure as well as to support.

i18n.hi: भटनागर और लिविंग्स्टन एक और खामोश चाल नोट करते हैं: अयनांत पर मंदिर की देह और परछाईं हैरतअंगेज़ नाप–तौल से चलती हैं। पत्थर मानो ढोता भी है, मापता भी।

panels.shot: wide dusk shot, devotees, dancers and water reflecting temple
panels.action: At dusk, the sabhamandapa is alive with dancers and musicians, the broad steps of the kunda filled with watchers; torches flicker and their light trembles in the water, reflecting the temple’s silhouette.

dialogue.text: The sabhamandapa was a hall of gathering and performance. Here ritual, recitation and dance unfolded, facing both water and shrine, the Sun’s axis binding crowd, king and cosmos.

i18n.hi: सभामंडप जुटान और प्रदर्शन का आँगन था। यहीं पूजा, पाठ और नृत्य खुलते, जल और गर्भ दोनों की ओर मुख किए, सूर्य की धुरी भीड़, राजा और ब्रह्मांड को एक डोरी में बाँधती।

panels.shot: mid shot of Bhima listening to recitation with temple behind
panels.action: Bhima I sits quietly on the mandapa steps among his people at twilight, listening to a priest recite, the layered silhouette of the temple rising intact behind them against the deepening sky.

dialogue.text: Chronicles of the time recall Bhima’s anxieties in a troubled age, yet at Modhera the inscriptional voice is of donors and craftsmen, fixed on the task of binding their world to a course of light.

i18n.hi: समय के वृत्तांत भीम के अशांत दिनों की घबराहट याद करते हैं, पर मोढेरा में शिलालेखों की आवाज़ दानियों और कारीगरों की है, जो अपनी दुनिया को रोशनी की एक धारा से बाँधने में तल्लीन थे।

panels.shot: high angle on collapsed shikhara over sanctum, present-day ruin state
panels.action: Centuries later, the viewer sees the temple sanctum roofless, its shikhara gone, broken stones scattered around while sturdy walls and carved pillars still stand against a bright Gujarat sky.

dialogue.text: The soaring shikhara over Modhera’s sanctum has long since fallen. No inscription names the cause. What remains is enough to show the original ambition of line, volume and light.

i18n.hi: मोढेरा के गर्भ पर उठी ऊँची शिखर अब बहुत पहले ढह चुकी। कोई शिलालेख कारण नहीं कहता। जो बचा है, वही रेखा, आयतन और रोशनी की पुरानी महत्वाकांक्षा दिखाने को काफी है।

panels.shot: low interior present-day shot from sanctum floor toward sunrise
panels.action: From the present-day sanctum floor, worn but clean, a visitor stands where the deity once stood, watching the orange disc of the rising sun framed exactly in the doorway and the hall beyond.

dialogue.text: Yet the equinox beam still finds its path. Without text, without priest, the daily experiment repeats: if you stand where the murti stood, the sun still reaches you.

i18n.hi: फिर भी विषुव की किरण अपना रास्ता ढूँढ लेती है। बिना शास्त्र, बिना पुजारी, रोज़ का प्रयोग दोहरता है: जहाँ मूर्ति थी, वहाँ खड़े हो, सूरज अब भी तुम्हें छू लेता है।

panels.shot: wide contemporary shot of tourists and archaeologists around kunda and temple
panels.action: Modern visitors, including archaeologists with notebooks and survey tripods, move across the kunda steps and temple plinth, the ancient carvings catching sunlight as people test alignments with quiet fascination.

dialogue.text: Archaeologists like Sankalia and Dhaky came with tape and transit, not incense. They traced measurements, checked orientations, and wrote down what the builders had left encoded in plan and profile.

i18n.hi: संकालिया और ढाकी जैसे पुरातत्ववेत्ता फूल नहीं, फीता और थियोडोलाइट लेकर आए। उन्होंने नाप खींचे, दिशाएँ जाँचीं, और जो शिल्पियों ने योजना और प्रोफ़ाइल में छुपा छोड़ा था, उसे लिख डाला।

panels.shot: intimate close-up of weathered sthapati statue or symbolic craftsman hands on stone
panels.action: A symbolic, almost timeless frame shows an elderly craftsman’s hands resting on a sun-warmed temple stone, calloused fingers following the crisp line of a carved sun-disc on the wall.

dialogue.text: We do not have the sthapatis’ own words, only their choices in stone. At Modhera, those choices show craft joined with observation, devotion joined with design, until sunrise itself became part of the temple.

i18n.hi: हमारे पास स्थापतियों के अपने शब्द नहीं, सिर्फ पत्थर में की गई उनकी चुनौतियाँ हैं। मोढेरा में ये चुनाव दिखाते हैं: शिल्प ने अवलोकन का हाथ थामा, भक्ति ने रूपांकन का, जब तक कि सूर्योदय खुद मंदिर का हिस्सा न बन गया।

title_i18n.hi: मोढेरा पढ़ता जमी हुई सुबह की लाली

subtitle_i18n.en: When Solanki stone learned to follow the sun
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब चालुक्य पत्थर ने सूरज का पीछा करना सीखा
